newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up on technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up on technical rebound.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index closed up on Tuesday due to a technical rebound helped by institutional support buying mainly in big firms, brokers said.
The index rose 1.242 points or 2.01 percent to 63.023 points, on volume of 14.8 million shares worth $7.2 million against $6.6 million on Monday.
Brokers said the main institutions pushed the index above the key 63-point resistance level in the last few minutes in order to help the listing of the new B share, Shanghai Kaikai, on Wednesday.

Brokers said institutions were seen supporting shares with a heavy weighting on the index including the market barometer, real estate developer Lujiazui, which has suffered sharp losses in recent days.
"But follow-up buying was limited despite institutional support," a broker said. "Most investors believe the rise is only a technical rebound with limited upward potential."
"The index is likely to fall again after the rebound," a second broker said. "No fresh capital is expected to flow into the market for now."
Of 42 B shares, 40 traded with 24 up, four flat and 12 down. Lujiazui was the most actively traded, ending up $0.026 or 3.7 percent at $0.866, on volume of 3.7 million shares.
Shanghai Tyre followed on institutional speculative buying, jumping $0.034 or 9.28 percent to $0.400, on volume of 45,000 shares.

Shanghai's A share market was up sharply on rumours that Beijing would cut interest rates and bank reserve ratios later this year, but brokers said the rebound would be short-lived given the heavy unwinding selling apparent at higher levels, brokers said.

The A index ended up 22.729 points or 2.49 percent at 936.570 points, on volume of 217.7 million shares worth 1.8 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index gained 54.994 points or 2.34 percent to 2405.639 points.
Anshan Trust was the star on talk of possible cuts in interest rates, jumping to its 10 percent limit-up of 9.57 yuan on volume of 6.7 million shares.
